description: Deliberate improvements in the Rust build over C# 2026.10.05: answers that are meant to differ. Policy (parity/README.md, Intentional diffs): one entry per reviewed change, never a wildcard over all requests; "requests" names the requests (globs allowed inside one corpus file), "aspects" the parts that differ, and "lines" (regexes) pins what the diff says, so a different change on the same answer still fails. "reason" says why the Rust answer is better, "backlog" the group, and "reviewed" who approved it and when ("Brandon 2026-10-08"). An entry without "reviewed" is only proposed: the diff lists it as not reviewed and still counts the request as unexplained. A change a user or an app can see needs Brandon by name. Each entry also gets a row in docs/rust-migration/known-diffs.md.

lines: ^\$\.error: only in B \(Sign in with your Navidrome admin account first\.\)$
^\+\{"error":"Sign in with your Navidrome admin account first\."\}$
diffs.reason: The recovery code is for fixing settings. The C# explicit marking asked UserOf, so a recovery-code session could read, start and cancel it and write explicit marks into music files; the Rust gate refuses a recovery session on every library-file route (LIBRARY_FILE_ROUTES) with the words those routes already answered.
diffs.knownDiff: Admin sign-in: the recovery code and library files

lines: ^\$\.error: .+ != Retype the Lidarr API key for the new address\.$
^\+\{"ok":false,"error":"Retype the Lidarr API key for the new address\."\}$
diffs.reason: The C# sent the saved Lidarr key to whatever address the test named; the Rust build sends it only to the saved address, as a save already does, and asks for the key to be typed for a new one.
diffs.knownDiff: `lidarr/test` and the saved key

diffs.reason: The C# showed a set secret as one bullet per character, up to 16, which told its length; the Rust build shows eight bullets for every set secret. These answers also list the charts plan's two settings (entry charts-settings-listed), which moves every key after GeneratedPlaylists:PopularNow two places on; those lines are pinned here too.
diffs.knownDiff: `config-sources` secrets

diffs.reason: Undoing an ISRC retag takes the code off the file, as the undo's own answer (isrc: null) says. C# 2026.10.05 left it there: LibraryTagEdits.Set wrote the ISRC through SetText, which returns on an empty value. Fixed in the port only (Brandon, 2026-10-07); group F's LibraryTagEdits.write clears it through tag_writer_extras::set_or_clear_text (G3). Navidrome then lists the removed copy without the code (remove-copy-seen, G4 R).
diffs.knownDiff: Clearing a tag field

diffs.reason: A cover run resumed after a stop counts each album and song once, and goes on with only what the stop left undone. C# 2026.10.05 ran the stopped batch again and counted it again (CoverUpgrade.cs:696,744): the picked preview of 3 albums ended with albumsDone 6, songsRead 20 of 10, kept and files doubled; a replace also counted an album it had written as kept. Fixed in the port only (Brandon, 2026-10-07). The run's reason line may also differ: see cover-run-reason-cleared (the C# left its last bulk-match line there by a race).
diffs.knownDiff: Cover upgrade: a resumed run's counts

diffs.reason: The cover scan leaves the trash folder out: C# 2026.10.05 walked into /music/.octo-trash and listed a song deleted from disk in 20-library-edits as an album of its own (one more album, song and soft row, and the sorted preview shifted by one). Fixed in the port only (Brandon, 2026-10-07). Until group F's delete and put back land, this request also differs for F's sake. The albumsDone line also carries the second port fix on this answer: albums done are counted the way albums in all are (the C# ended 6 of 5; known-diffs "Cover upgrade: albums done and albums in all").
diffs.knownDiff: Library walks and the trash

diffs.reason: A picked cover run that matched its albums in bulk ends with no reason line, as the C# meant (its finally sets Reason = null). C# 2026.10.05 reported the bulk match's progress through Progress<string>, which runs the update later on the thread pool, so the last line ("barcodes 1 of 1 · Apple matched 1") could land after the finally and stay on the finished run; whether it did changed from run to run (17-covers-explicit/covers-resumed-done had it in one C# recording and not in another).
diffs.knownDiff: Cover upgrade: the bulk match's last line

diffs.reason: The C# saved slskd's web address (the Open slskd link) with the spaces it was typed with, and the settings answer and the form showed them; the Rust build saves and reads it trimmed. These answers also list the charts plan's two chart settings (entry charts-settings-listed); those lines are pinned here too.
diffs.knownDiff: slskd's web address saved with spaces

diffs.reason: Keep as playlist works. The C# sent the playlist create as application/json; charset=utf-8, which Navidrome 0.64.2 reads as an M3U import: an empty playlist named after the time, an M3U answer the C# could not read, a 500 for the person, and another empty playlist every 30 s pass while the switch stayed on. The port sends application/json exactly, so the playlist is named after the list, holds its songs, belongs to the list's owner, and the list remembers it; a failed sync deletes what it made and backs off.
diffs.knownDiff: Spotify import: Keep as playlist

diffs.reason: getTopChart takes chart (the overall chart, Best New Songs, Trending Songs or an Apple genre; the charts plan, Brandon 2026-10-07), so a chart's answer says which chart it is, its name and the country it was read for (null while Apple's country is not known). Added fields only: old apps send no chart and read the old ones. The explicitStatus lines on the same answers are group P's.
diffs.knownDiff: `getTopChart`

diffs.reason: octoTopSongs version 2 tells an app that getTopChart takes chart and getCharts lists the country's charts (the charts plan, Brandon 2026-10-07); version 1 is still listed, so an app that knows only that one keeps working. The other lines on these answers are other groups': octoAcquisitions [1, 2] and the octoImports entry the port has not reached yet.
diffs.knownDiff: `octoTopSongs`

lines: ^\$\.command: git fetch --tags && git checkout --detach \S+ && \(docker compose pull yt-dlp-shim octo-sonic \|\| docker compose .* != git fetch --tags && git checkout --detach \S+ && \(docker compose pull octo yt-dlp-shim octo-sonic \|\| .*$
diffs.reason: Octo is pulled from this release on (the bridge release, shipped with the Rust one): docker compose build octo builds nothing, so the hand command pulls Octo with its sidecars and builds the -source services only when the pull fails. reinstallCommand is what the card shows when the update helper is older than version 2, which would otherwise restart the same Octo and call it an update.
diffs.knownDiff: Update card: Octo pulled, helper version 2

diffs.reason: The charts plan's two settings (Brandon 2026-10-07: chart lists beyond Popular right now, read for one country) are settings like the others: GET settings, a save's persisted answer, Raw config and the settings file list GeneratedPlaylists.Charts (the chart lists to make, empty for the default set) and GeneratedPlaylists.ChartCountry (auto by default), and config-sources lists their keys. C# 2026.10.05 has neither. A Raw config save that writes them back is 46 bytes longer. Values only added; no other setting changes.
diffs.knownDiff: Chart settings in the settings answers

^\+\{"ok":false,"error":"Could\ not\ connect\ to\ stubs:9:\ the\ connection\ was\ refused\."\}$
diffs.reason: A failed call says what happened in plain words instead of .NET's exception text (BACKLOG, Improvements we want while porting): "Could not connect to stubs:9: the connection was refused." for "Connection refused (stubs:9)", and likewise a timeout ("No answer came within 100 seconds, so Octo stopped waiting."), a name that cannot be looked up and a status that is not a success ("The server answered 404 (Not Found)."). The Lidarr test is the one answer the corpus reaches.
diffs.knownDiff: Plain error words

diffs.reason: Popular right now's row carries octoCoverTitle "Popular" so the Octo apps draw "Popular" over "Chart" at full title size, as the server's own cover now does. A list name ending in Mix, Radio or Chart reads as two lines whatever kind of list it is ("Discovery Mix" is "Discovery" over "Mix"); no corpus request draws such a cover, so only the row field shows.
diffs.knownDiff: List covers: the kind word and Popular

diffs.reason: Two new library actions, Wrong lyrics and Wrong cover, appended after Keep (the journal stores actions as numbers). Every settings answer lists all actions, so the list grows from five to seven (both new ones off, with no star), and libraryAction's unknown-action message names the two new app names, lyrics and cover-swap. The lines are estimated; they are pinned on the first parity run at integration.
diffs.knownDiff: Wrong lyrics and Wrong cover actions

diffs.reason: An outside song's size is the true byte count of the stream Octo relays, learned from the shim (yt-dlp's filesize, the URL's clen when that is unknown, and the bytes of a play over both), and absent until it is known. The C# native rows sent duration x bit rate as the size, an estimate that never matched the bytes; strict clients use the size to seek. Subsonic rows (search3 and the rest) gain the true size once known, so a corpus row whose stream the parity stub never sized is unchanged there. The lines need pinning against a parity run.
diffs.knownDiff: Outside songs: the true stream size

lines: ^\$\.meaning:\ Keeps\ the\ best\ copy\ of\ each\ song,\ fills\ in\ the\ tags\ it\ lacks\ from\ the\ others,\ and\ moves\ the\ others\ to\ the\ server's\ tr\.\.\.\ !=\ Keeps\ the\ best\ sound\ of\ each\ song\ in\ the\ copy\ people\ starred,\ rated,\ played\ or\ put\ in\ playlists,\ fills\ in\ the\ tags\ it\.\.\.$
diffs.reason: Fixing duplicates keeps the best sound in the copy people marked: the copy whose id carries the most stars, ratings and plays (then playlist entries, then the oldest) keeps its id and path, and the best-sounding copy of the same format moves into it under its identity tags. Duplicates' fix meaning says so, a set in the list notes that Fix these copies picks the marked copy, and the preview's side by side view marks the copy whose sound moves in ("sound"). With the planted Harbor Lights pair (FLAC and MP3, nobody's marks) the plan itself stays the best-sound one.
diffs.knownDiff: Duplicates keep the marked copy's id

diffs.reason: Lidarr's webhook (POST /api/lidarr/webhook) is off until Lidarr.WebhookSecret is set, the password Lidarr's Webhook connection sends. It is a credential like the Lidarr API key: GET settings, a save's persisted answer and Raw config list it masked (blank when unset), config-sources lists Lidarr:WebhookSecret as a secret, so every key after it moves one place on. C# 2026.10.05 has neither the setting nor the route. The lines are proposed from the shape of the charts entry and must be confirmed against the parity run at integration, together with the index pins of config-sources-fixed-mask that this key shifts.
diffs.knownDiff: Lidarr webhook password in the settings answers

diffs.reason: Soulseek is optional: Soulseek.Enabled (true by default) turns it off even with an address set, and a blank address is off too. GET settings, a save's persisted answer and Raw config list it, and config-sources lists Soulseek:Enabled, so every key after it moves one place on. C# 2026.10.05 has no such setting and called http://localhost:5030 without an address. The lines are proposed from the shape of the charts entry and must be confirmed against the parity run at integration, together with lidarr-webhook-secret-listed (the config-sources count here assumes both keys).
diffs.knownDiff: Soulseek is optional

diffs.reason: LB Radio has a difficulty setting (easy, medium or hard; easy by default, which is what C# 2026.10.05 always asked for): GET settings, a save's persisted answer, Raw config and the settings file list RadioSources.ListenBrainzRadioMode after ListenBrainzAlgorithm, and config-sources lists its key (180). Values only added; no other setting changes. The lines were written ahead of a parity run; the integration run pins the exact diff lines, a Raw config save's byte count included.
diffs.knownDiff: ListenBrainz radio difficulty in the settings answers

diffs.reason: Every settings answer (settings, raw-config, config-sources, a save's persisted copy, settings.json) now carries all of the new keys at once: GeneratedPlaylists Charts and ChartCountry, LikedSongs, LikedSongsName and LikedSongsMax, CountryMixes, Countries, MaxCountryPlaylists and CountryLookupsPerRefresh, Lidarr WebhookSecret, Soulseek Enabled, RadioSources ListenBrainzRadioMode and the two new LibraryActions (seven actions), with the config-sources rows they shift and the trimmed slskd web address. One answer can be explained by one entry only, so the single-change entries (charts-settings-listed, liked-songs-first, country-mix-settings, lidarr-webhook-secret-listed, soulseek-enabled-listed, lb-radio-mode-listed, wrong-lyrics-wrong-cover-actions, config-sources-fixed-mask, slskd-web-url-trimmed) no longer match these answers; this entry pins the combined diff line by line.
diffs.knownDiff: Settings answers with every new key
